subject: Re: DPA redlines — embeddings retention, logs & EU-US transfer
messages:
From: Julia Barnes <julia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redlines and questions on roles and transfers

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the DPA. Attached is our redline (Acme-DPA-redline-20260610.docx). A few high-level items we flagged that we need clarified before legal can sign:

- Controller vs Processor: Acme views customer data as controller data. We want explicit clarifications in Section 2 that embeddings derived from customer input remain customer data and that any model training/derivative use requires separate consent.
- Logs and telemetry: we need retention caps for request/response logs (max 90 days), plus clear delete commands for backups.
- International transfers: Acme requires either updated EU Standard Contractual Clauses or an explicit mechanism for EU->US transfers; please confirm Redwood's stance and whether you will include the SCC addendum.
- Subprocessors: please provide the latest subprocessor list and confirm 30-day notice for new subprocessors.

We appreciate the quick turn — can someone on your side review and propose language for the embeddings and logs items?

Best,
Julia
Legal Counsel | Acme Corp

Subject: Re: DPA redlines and questions on roles and transfers

Julia — thanks, we got the redline and have started an internal review. Quick notes from product & legal triage:

- Embeddings/derivatives: Redwood's standard position is that embeddings produced from customer inputs are "derived customer data" retained per customer-configured retention policy. We do not use customer content to train public models unless a customer opts into that program. We can propose explicit language that embeddings remain under customer control and that any use for model improvements requires opt-in.

- Logs & telemetry: our default retention for request/response logs is 30 days, with options up to 365 days under dedicated contracts. We can offer a 90-day cap for Acme's ACME-RW-2026-05 scope. Need to confirm if Acme requires deletion certification for backups.

- International transfers: Redwood supports SCCs; we can attach an SCC addendum and sign it. For customers wanting on-prem or EU-only hosting, we can discuss Private deployment.

- Subprocessors: we will attach the current subprocessor list; Redwood gives 30-day notice for materially new subprocessors.

I'm looping in Monica (sales lead) and Rishi (privacy) to propose redline text for the embeddings and logs items and to coordinate DocuSign.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

1) If we agree to 90-day logs retention, Redwood will include an audit log export for the contract term at no additional charge.
2) For embeddings, if Acme requires a strict no-derivative-use clause (no internal model improvements), we may need to scope SLAs around possible latency/cost impacts if caching/quantization options are restricted.

I'll defer to Rishi on precise legal language. Once we have agreed text, I'll initiate DocuSign (we can route to your legal and signers). Are you able to confirm primary signatory and whether they prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign?

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Julia Barnes <julia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T11:18:00Z
Subject: Proposed DPA language for embeddings, logs, and transfers

Julia — attaching suggested redline snippets below. Happy to iterate.

1) Controller vs Processor / Embeddings
Proposed clause:
"For clarity, Customer data refers to all input data provided by Customer. Derivative artifacts (including but not limited to embeddings, feature vectors, metadata aggregations) generated from Customer data in the course of providing the Service shall be treated as Customer data and shall not be used for model training, model improvement, or other research purposes unless Customer provides explicit, documented opt-in consent. Redwood will enforce tenant isolation for such derivative artifacts and make deletion endpoints available as set out in Section X."

2) Logs and telemetry
Proposed clause:
"Redwood will retain request/response logs and telemetry for a period no longer than 90 days for the Services provided under this Agreement, unless Customer requests an alternative retention period in writing. Redwood will purge backups containing Customer data within 120 days of deletion requests where feasible and will provide certification of deletion upon Customer's request subject to reasonable operational constraints."

3) International transfers / SCCs
Proposed clause:
"Data transfers from the EEA to the United States in connection with the performance of the Services shall be governed by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in effect at the time of transfer. Redwood will append an SCC addendum to this Agreement and execute it contemporaneously with the DPA signature."

Notes: we recommend adding a schedule that lists current subprocessors and a 30-day notice commitment for changes. Evelyn — can you attach the current subprocessor list and SCC addendum draft?

-Rishi
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
